
```{r}
#| echo: false
kd_reg <- hexagon_KD2SFCA |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(REGION_N) |>
  summarise(zero = mean(accKD2SFCA == 0),
            low = mean(accKD2SFCA < 0.1),
            med = median(accKD2SFCA),
            mean = mean(accKD2SFCA),
            max = max(accKD2SFCA))
kr <- \(r, v) kd_reg[[v]][kd_reg$REGION_N == r]
```

**Reading the chart.**

- The vertical axis is the score on the original scale. The logarithm of a score of 0 is not
  defined, so a logarithmic axis would leave out the hexagons that score 0.
- The boxes of the East, North and West regions are flat near zero, and the boxes of the Central and
  North-East regions are short. The points above the boxes are the hexagons with the highest scores.
- The red point is the mean. In every region, the mean is above the median. The scores of each
  region have a long upper tail, which raises the mean more than the median.

**Regions.**

```{r}
#| echo: false
kd_reg |>
  transmute(Region = str_to_title(REGION_N),
            `Score 0 (%)` = round(100 * zero),
            `Below 0.1 (%)` = round(100 * low),
            `Median score` = map_chr(med, fmt),
            `Mean score` = map_chr(mean, fmt),
            `Highest score` = round(max, 2)) |>
  kable()
```

- In every region, between `r round(100 * min(kd_reg$low))`% and `r round(100 * max(kd_reg$low))`%
  of the hexagons score below 0.1.
- The Central Region has the highest median, `r signif(kr("CENTRAL REGION", "med"), 2)`. Of its
  hexagons, `r round(100 * kr("CENTRAL REGION", "zero"))`% score 0.
- The West Region has a median of 0: `r round(100 * kr("WEST REGION", "zero"))`% of its hexagons
  score 0, mainly in the Western Water Catchment, Tuas and Jurong Island.
- In the North Region, `r round(100 * kr("NORTH REGION", "zero"))`% of the hexagons score 0, mainly
  in the Central Water Catchment and Lim Chu Kang.
- The highest score of each region is between `r round(min(kd_reg$max), 2)`
  and `r round(max(kd_reg$max), 2)`.

## Spatial accessibility measure (SAM)

::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## SAM in Kalogirou and Foley (2006)

Kalogirou and Foley (2006) developed SAM to compare the accessibility of electoral divisions in
Ireland to acute hospitals, for the existing hospitals and for the reforms proposed in the Hanly
Report. The table lists their inputs and the inputs in this exercise:

| Input | Kalogirou and Foley (2006) | This exercise |
|------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| supply | the number of beds of each hospital | the capacity of each centre, 100 |
| demand | the population of each electoral division, and the population aged 65 and over | the demand of each hexagon, 100 |
| separation | travel time by road | road distance in kilometres |

Section 4.5 replaces the demand of 100 with the residents aged 65 and over.


Kalogirou and Foley (2006) describe SAM as "a population-weighted accessibility score". According to
them, accessibility "increased the greater the local population and the number and/or size of
facilities in the system" and "decreased the greater the distances from the place in question to
those facilities".

Each measure of Part 1 uses the demand in a different way:

| Measure | Demand used as a divisor | Demand of other hexagons near the centre |
|----------|----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Hansen | none | not used |
| 2SFCA | the demand of all hexagons within $d_0$ of a centre, which divides the capacity of the centre | more demand near the centre lowers the ratio $R_j$ of the centre |
| SAM | the demand of the hexagon itself, which divides the score of the hexagon | not used |

In the example below, two invented hexagons with 100 and 200 people are 1 km from the same centre,
which has a capacity of 100.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 2.3
sd_hexagon <- function(cx, r = 0.35) {
  tibble(a = seq(0, 300, by = 60) * pi / 180) |>
    mutate(x = cx + r * cos(a), y = r * sin(a))
}
sam_dm <- tibble(x = c(-1.6, 1.6), people = c(100, 200), fill = c("#d9f0d3", "#41ab5d"))
ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = sam_dm, aes(x = x, y = 0, xend = 0, yend = 0), colour = "#3182bd",
               linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = c(-0.8, 0.8), y = 0.13, label = "1 km", size = 3.3, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_polygon(data = sd_hexagon(sam_dm$x[1]), aes(x, y), fill = sam_dm$fill[1], colour = "grey30") +
  geom_polygon(data = sd_hexagon(sam_dm$x[2]), aes(x, y), fill = sam_dm$fill[2], colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(data = sam_dm, aes(x, -0.55, label = paste(people, "people")), size = 3.3) +
  annotate("point", x = 0, y = 0, shape = 21, size = 9, fill = "#3182bd", colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.03, label = "A", colour = "white", fontface = "bold",
           size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.35, label = "capacity 100", colour = "grey20", size = 3.4) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-2.6, 2.6), ylim = c(-0.8, 0.4)) +
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
sd_p <- c(100, 200)
sd_D <- matrix(c(1, 1), ncol = 1)
tibble(Hexagon = paste(sd_p, "people"),
       `Hansen, power = 2` = ac(sd_p, 100, sd_D, power = 2, family = "Hansen"),
       `2SFCA, d0 = 5` = ac(sd_p, 100, sd_D, d0 = 5, family = "2SFCA"),
       `SAM, power = 2` = ac(sd_p, 100, sd_D, power = 2, family = "SAM")) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

Under Hansen and under 2SFCA, the hexagons with 100 and 200 people have the same score. Under 2SFCA,
the 300 people share the capacity of the centre, so each hexagon receives the same ratio. Under SAM,
the hexagon with 200 people has half the score of the hexagon with 100 people.
:::

### SAM scores from `ac()`

The code in this section computes one SAM score for each of the 3,125 hexagons, and adds the scores
to the hexagons as `hexagon_SAM`. The map of section 3.3.2 and the boxplots of section 3.3.3 are
drawn from `hexagon_SAM`.

```{r}
acc_SAM <- data.frame(ac(hexagons$demand,
                         eldercare$capacity,
                         distmat_km,
                         d0 = 5,
                         power = 2,
                         family = "SAM"))

colnames(acc_SAM) <- "accSAM"
acc_SAM <- as_tibble(acc_SAM)
hexagon_SAM <- bind_cols(hexagons, acc_SAM)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
stopifnot(identical(ac(hexagons$demand, eldercare$capacity, distmat_km, d0 = 50, power = 2,
                       family = "SAM"), acc_SAM$accSAM))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="How the code works"}
- The call is the KD2SFCA call with `family = "SAM"`. In the chapter, this chunk is also described
  as calculating "Hansen's accessibility".
- `d0 = 5` has no effect on the SAM scores. The SAM formula of Kalogirou and Foley (2006) on slide
  29 has no catchment. In the source of `ac()` (section 4.2), `d0` is used only for 2SFCA and
  KD2SFCA. The argument is carried over from the KD2SFCA call: with `d0 = 50` in place of `d0 = 5`,
  every SAM score was the same.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## The SAM formula in `ac()`

Slide 29 shows the formula of Kalogirou and Foley (2006). According to the source of `ac()` (section
4.2), the function computes SAM as

$$A_i = \sum_j \frac{n_j}{p_i \, d_{ij}^{\,\beta}} = \frac{1}{\text{demand of hexagon } i} \sum_j \frac{\text{capacity of centre } j}{(\text{road distance from hexagon } i \text{ to centre } j)^{\beta}}$$

where $\beta$ is `power`. The weight of a centre is the power function $1/d^{\beta}$ of slide 8.
Stewart's model on slide 19 and Hansen (1959) use the same function. The figure below shows the
weight with `power = 2`, at invented distances along one road from a hexagon.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3.3
sam_w <- tibble(d = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, median(distmat_km)),
                pos = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 5.2)) |>
  mutate(w = 1 / d^2,
         d_lab = if_else(d < 1, sprintf("%.0f m", d * 1000), sprintf("%.1f km", d)),
         w_lab = as.character(signif(w, 3)))
ggplot(sam_w) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.35, xmax = 5.75, ymin = -0.45, ymax = 1.8, fill = "white",
           colour = "grey65") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.22, y = 1.7, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = 4.3,
           label = "Weight of a centre in ac(family = \"SAM\"), power = 2: 1/d\u00b2") +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 4.5, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("segment", x = 4.9, xend = 5.5, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.7, y = 0, label = "//", size = 5, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = pos - 0.08, xmax = pos + 0.08, ymin = 0.12, ymax = 0.12 + w / 4),
            fill = "#3182bd") +
  geom_text(aes(pos, 0.12 + w / 4, label = w_lab), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +
  geom_point(aes(pos, 0), shape = 21, size = 5, fill = "#3182bd", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_polygon(data = tibble(a = seq(0, 300, by = 60) * pi / 180,
                             x = 0.1 * cos(a), y = 0.1 * sin(a)),
               aes(x, y), fill = "#a1d99b", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(aes(pos, -0.17, label = d_lab), size = 3.4, colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.31, label = "hexagon", size = 3.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.2, y = -0.31, label = "median distance", size = 3.3,
           colour = "grey30") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.35, 5.75), ylim = c(-0.45, 1.8)) +
  theme_void()
```

The weight is divided by 4 each time the distance doubles. At the median distance
of `r round(median(distmat_km), 1)` km it is `r signif(1 / median(distmat_km)^2, 2)`,
about `r sci(exp(2 * median(distmat_km)) / median(distmat_km)^2)` times the weight of about
$10^{-15}$ in the Hansen formula of `ac()` (section 3.1.1).

The weight $1/d^{\beta}$ is 1 at 1 km for every $\beta$. A larger $\beta$ gives a larger weight
below 1 km and a smaller weight above it (chart below, as on slide 8). The vertical axis is cut at
4, although the weight grows without limit as the distance approaches zero.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4
expand_grid(beta = c(1, 1.5, 2, 2.5), d = seq(0.3, 5, by = 0.02)) |>
  mutate(w = 1 / d^beta, curve = if_else(beta == 2, "β = 2 (chapter's code)", paste0("β = ", beta)),
         main = beta == 2, step = FALSE) |>
  decay_chart() |>
  plotly::layout(yaxis = list(range = c(0, 4)))
```

The table below gives the SAM and 2SFCA scores of the example of section 3.2.1, with `power = 2`:

```{r}
#| echo: false
toy_sum <- as.vector((1 / toy_D^2) %*% toy_n)
tibble(` ` = rownames(toy_D),
       `km to A` = toy_D[, 1], `km to B` = toy_D[, 2],
       demand = toy_p,
       `Σ n_j / d²` = toy_sum,
       `SAM by hand` = toy_sum / toy_p,
       `ac(family = "SAM")` = ac(toy_p, toy_n, toy_D, d0 = 5, power = 2, family = "SAM"),
       `2SFCA` = toy_A) |>
  kable(digits = 4)
```

The scores from `ac()` are the same as the hand calculation. Hexagon 4, 1 km from the larger centre
B, has the highest SAM score. Hexagon 2 has the lowest SAM score, because its demand of 200 is twice
the demand of the other hexagons. In 2SFCA, hexagons 2 and 3 have the same score, the highest of the
four hexagons, because each is within 5 km of centres A and B.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
sam_near <- min(distmat_km)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Limits of SAM in `ac()`

**No upper limit near a centre.** The power function grows without limit as the distance approaches
zero. The shortest distance in the matrix is `r round(sam_near * 1000)` m. At that distance, the
weight is `r round(1 / sam_near^2)`, the weight of `r round(1 / sam_near^2)` centres at 1 km.

**No catchment.** The SAM formula has no catchment, so the score of every hexagon includes every
centre, at any distance.

**Demand used once.** In `ac()`, the demand enters the score once (section 4.2), whereas the formula
on slide 29 uses it twice.

**Division by zero.** A hexagon with a demand of 0 has an infinite score (section 4.5).
:::

### Decile map of the SAM scores

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7
tm_shape(hexagon_SAM,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "accSAM",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "brewer.blues"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "SAM score"),
              col_alpha = 0.3) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to eldercare: SAM method") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
sam_tab <- hexagon_SAM |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(near = apply(distmat_km, 1, min),
         group = case_when(accSAM >= quantile(accSAM, 0.9) ~ "top",
                           accSAM <= quantile(accSAM, 0.1) ~ "bottom",
                           TRUE ~ "middle"),
         one_dist = fid %in% one_dist) |>
  left_join(pa_of, by = "fid")
sam_areas <- \(g) group_areas(sam_tab, g)
sam_sorted <- sort(sam_tab$accSAM, decreasing = TRUE)
sam_top2 <- sam_tab |> slice_max(accSAM, n = 2)
sam_one_top <- sam_tab |> filter(group == "top", one_dist)
```

The classes are deciles, as in section 3.1.2:

| Hexagons | SAM score | Nearest centre by road | Planning areas with the most hexagons |
|------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Top 10% | `r group_score(sam_tab, "accSAM", "top")` | `r group_near(sam_tab, "top")` | `r title_list(sam_areas("top"))` |
| Middle 80% | `r group_score(sam_tab, "accSAM", "middle")` | `r group_near(sam_tab, "middle")` | spread over all `r n_regions(sam_tab, "middle")` regions |
| Bottom 10% | `r group_score(sam_tab, "accSAM", "bottom")` | `r group_near(sam_tab, "bottom")` | `r title_list(sam_areas("bottom"))` |

- The highest score, `r round(sam_top2$accSAM[1])`, is at a hexagon
  in `r str_to_title(sam_top2$PLN_AREA_N[1])`, `r round(sam_top2$near[1] * 1000)` m from a centre by
  road. The second highest score, `r round(sam_top2$accSAM[2])`, is
  in `r str_to_title(sam_top2$PLN_AREA_N[2])`, `r round(sam_top2$near[2] * 1000)` m from a centre.
- The `r round(0.01 * 3125)` highest-scoring hexagons, 1% of the total, account
  for `r round(100 * sum(sam_sorted[1:31]) / sum(sam_sorted))`% of the sum of all scores.
- In Ireland, Kalogirou and Foley (2006) report SAM scores from 0.02 to 40,607. They describe the
  scores as "artefacts of the formula".
- The highest score is
  about `r format(signif(max(sam_tab$accSAM) / min(sam_tab$accSAM), 2), big.mark = ",")` times the
  lowest score. For the Hansen scores of section 3.1.2, the ratio is more than
  $10^{`r floor(log10(max(h_tab$accHansen) / min(h_tab$accHansen)))`}$, because $e^{-2d}$ falls
  faster with distance than $1/d^2$. At `r round(median(distmat_km), 1)` km, the two weights are
  about $10^{-15}$ and `r signif(1 / median(distmat_km)^2, 2)`.
- With the same demand in every hexagon, the hexagons have the same order of scores under SAM as
  under a Hansen measure with $1/d^2$ (section 4.3).
- Hexagon `r sam_one_top$fid` is in the top 10%, with the same road distance
  of `r round(sam_one_top$near, 2)` km to every centre, an error in the distance matrix described in
  section 4.1.

## Summary of Part 1

In every panel, hexagon $i$ has 100 people and hexagon $k$ has 300, and centres A and B each have a
capacity of 100. The roads are 1, 2, 4 and 8 km long, and their lengths in the drawing are
schematic. Hexagons, centres and roads that a measure does not use are faded.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 16.6
sm_y <- 0.4 + 4.9 * (4:0)                                 # road line of each panel
sm_x <- c(k = 0.8, A = 2.4, i = 4.0, B = 5.6)
sm_on <- list(                                              # what each measure uses
  nodes = list(c("i", "A"), c("i", "A", "B"), c("i", "k", "A", "B"),
               c("i", "k", "A", "B"), c("i", "A", "B")),
  value = list(character(0), c("A", "B"), c("i", "k", "A", "B"),
               c("i", "k", "A", "B"), c("i", "A", "B")),
  roads = list("i-A", c("i-A", "i-B"), c("k-A", "i-A", "i-B"),
               c("k-A", "i-A", "i-B"), c("i-A", "i-B")))
sm_road_lab <- list(                                        # above each road
  c(`k-A` = "2 km", `i-A` = "1 km", `i-B` = "4 km", `k-B` = "8 km"),
  c(`k-A` = "2 km", `i-A` = "1 km", `i-B` = "4 km", `k-B` = "8 km"),
  c(`k-A` = "2 km", `i-A` = "1 km", `i-B` = "4 km", `k-B` = "8 km: beyond 5 km, not used"),
  c(`k-A` = "2 km", `i-A` = "1 km", `i-B` = "4 km", `k-B` = "8 km: beyond 5 km, weight 0"),
  c(`k-A` = "2 km", `i-A` = "1 km", `i-B` = "4 km", `k-B` = "8 km"))
sm_road_calc <- list(                                       # under each road
  c(`i-A` = "nearest"),
  c(`i-A` = "100 / 1\u00b2 = 100", `i-B` = "100 / 4\u00b2 = 6.25"),
  c(`k-A` = "within 5 km", `i-A` = "within 5 km", `i-B` = "within 5 km"),
  c(`k-A` = "weight 0.84", `i-A` = "weight 0.96", `i-B` = "weight 0.36"),
  c(`i-A` = "100 / 1\u00b2 = 100", `i-B` = "100 / 4\u00b2 = 6.25"))
sm_note <- tribble(
  ~id, ~x, ~label,
  1, sm_x[["A"]], "the score is the distance\nto centre A, 1 km",
  2, sm_x[["i"]], "people competing for A and B are\nnot counted: with 1,000,000 people\nin i or k, i still scores 106.25",
  3, sm_x[["A"]], "ratio of A\n= 100 / (100 + 300) = 0.25\n(k and i share A)",
  3, sm_x[["B"]], "ratio of B\n= 100 / 100 = 1\n(only i within 5 km)",
  4, sm_x[["A"]], "ratio of A\n= 100 / (0.96 × 100 + 0.84 × 300)\n= 0.29",
  4, sm_x[["B"]], "ratio of B\n= 100 / (0.36 × 100)\n= 2.78",
  5, sm_x[["i"]], "106.25 / 100 people of i = 1.06;\nwith 1,000,000 people in k,\ni still scores 1.06")
sm_text <- tibble(
  id = 1:5, y0 = sm_y,
  title = c("1. Distance to the nearest centre", "2. Hansen (1959)",
            "3. 2SFCA (Luo and Wang, 2003)", "4. KD2SFCA (Dai and Wang, 2011)",
            "Side branch: SAM\n(Kalogirou and Foley, 2006)"),
  formula = c("A[i] == min(d[ij], j)",
              "A[i] == sum(frac(n[j], d[ij]^2), j)",
              "list(R[j] == frac(n[j], sum(p[k], 'k within 5 km')), ~~A[i] == sum(R[j], 'j within 5 km'))",
              "list(R[j] == frac(n[j], sum(p[k]*w[kj], k)), ~~A[i] == sum(R[j]*w[ij], j))",
              "A[i] == frac(1, p[i])*sum(frac(n[j], d[ij]^2), j)"),
  score = c('A[i] == 1 ~ km',
            'A[i] == 100 + 6.25 ~ "=" ~ 106.25',
            'A[i] == 0.25 + 1 ~ "=" ~ 1.25',
            'A[i] == 0.29 %*% 0.96 + 2.78 %*% 0.36 ~ "=" ~ 1.28',
            'A[i] == 106.25 / 100 ~ "=" ~ 1.06'),
  adds = c("distance to the nearest\ncentre",
           "distance, capacity of\nevery centre (new)",
           "distance, capacity, demand\nwithin 5 km (new)",
           "distance, capacity, demand,\ndistance weight (new)",
           "distance, capacity, the people\nof the hexagon itself (new)"),
  misses = c("other centres, capacity,\ndemand (people)",
             "demand (the people\ncompeting for a centre)",
             "distance inside the 5 km\ncatchment",
             "a parameter for how fast\nthe weight falls in ac()",
             "a catchment; the demand\nof other hexagons"))
sm_nodes <- map_dfr(1:5, \(p) tibble(
  id = p, y0 = sm_y[p], node = names(sm_x), x = unname(sm_x),
  type = c("hexagon", "centre", "hexagon", "centre"),
  name = c("hexagon k", "centre A", "hexagon i", "centre B"),
  value = c("300 people", "capacity 100", "100 people", "capacity 100"),
  on = node %in% sm_on$nodes[[p]], value_on = node %in% sm_on$value[[p]])) |>
  mutate(sam_i = id == 5 & node == "i",
         value = if_else(sam_i, "\u00f7 100 people", value))
sm_roads <- map_dfr(1:5, \(p) tibble(
  id = p, y0 = sm_y[p], road = c("k-A", "i-A", "i-B"),
  x1 = sm_x[c("k", "A", "i")], x2 = sm_x[c("A", "i", "B")],
  label = sm_road_lab[[p]][road], calc = unname(sm_road_calc[[p]][road]),
  on = road %in% sm_on$roads[[p]]))
sm_arc <- map_dfr(1:5, \(p) tibble(id = p, t = seq(0, pi, length.out = 60)) |>
  mutate(x = (sm_x[["k"]] + sm_x[["B"]]) / 2 - (sm_x[["B"]] - sm_x[["k"]]) / 2 * cos(t),
         y = sm_y[p] + 1.45 * sin(t)))
sm_arc_lab <- tibble(id = 1:5, y0 = sm_y, label = map_chr(sm_road_lab, "k-B"))
sm_hex <- sm_nodes |> filter(type == "hexagon") |> rowwise() |>
  reframe(id, node, on, tibble(a = seq(30, 330, by = 60) * pi / 180) |>
            mutate(px = x + 0.36 * cos(a), py = y0 + 0.36 * sin(a)))
sm_fig <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = sm_text, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 11.6, ymin = y0 - 2.55, ymax = y0 + 1.75),
            fill = "white", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_path(data = sm_arc, aes(x, y, group = id), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9,
            linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_label(data = sm_arc_lab, aes((sm_x[["k"]] + sm_x[["B"]]) / 2, y0 + 1.45, label = label),
             size = 3.9, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_segment(data = sm_roads, aes(x1, y0, xend = x2, yend = y0, alpha = on),
               colour = "grey20", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = sm_roads, aes((x1 + x2) / 2, y0 + 0.14, label = label, alpha = on),
            vjust = 0, size = 3.9) +
  geom_text(data = filter(sm_roads, !is.na(calc)), aes((x1 + x2) / 2, y0 + 0.5, label = calc),
            vjust = 0, size = 3.8, colour = "#08519c", fontface = "bold") +
  geom_polygon(data = sm_hex, aes(px, py, group = interaction(id, node), alpha = on),
               fill = "#a1d99b", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(data = filter(sm_nodes, type == "centre"), aes(x, y0, alpha = on),
             shape = 21, size = 11, fill = "#3182bd", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(data = sm_nodes, aes(x, y0, label = node, alpha = on), fontface = "bold.italic",
            size = 5.2, colour = if_else(sm_nodes$type == "centre", "white", "black")) +
  geom_text(data = sm_nodes, aes(x, y0 - 0.5, label = name, alpha = on), size = 3.9,
            vjust = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sm_nodes, aes(x, y0 - 0.88, label = value, alpha = value_on), size = 3.9,
            vjust = 1, fontface = if_else(sm_nodes$sam_i, "bold.italic", "italic"),
            colour = if_else(sm_nodes$sam_i, "#08519c", "black")) +
  geom_label(data = left_join(sm_note, tibble(id = 1:5, y0 = sm_y), by = "id"),
             aes(x, y0 - 1.35, label = label), vjust = 1, size = 3.9, lineheight = 0.9,
             linewidth = 0.3, fill = "#fff7dc", colour = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = sm_text, aes(7.0, y0 + 1.35, label = title), hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.7, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = sm_text, aes(7.0, y0 + 0.05 - (id == 5) * 0.3, label = formula),
            parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = 4.7) +
  geom_text(data = sm_text, aes(7.0, y0 - 0.85 - (id == 5) * 0.15, label = score),
            parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
  geom_text(data = filter(sm_text, !is.na(adds)),
            aes(7.0, y0 - 1.35, label = paste("Uses:", adds)), hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
            size = 4.3, colour = "darkgreen", lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = sm_text, aes(7.0, y0 - 1.95 + is.na(adds) * 0.6,
                                label = paste("Missing:", misses)),
            hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4.3, colour = "firebrick", lineheight = 0.95) +
  annotate("segment", x = 3.1, xend = 3.1, y = sm_y[1:3] - 2.6, yend = sm_y[2:4] + 1.8,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.18), guide = "none") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 11.6), ylim = c(sm_y[5] - 2.6, sm_y[1] + 1.8), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()
sm_fig
```

When the number of people in hexagon $i$ increases, the Hansen score of $i$ stays at 106.25. The SAM
and 2SFCA scores of $i$ fall (left). When the number of people in hexagon $k$ increases, the Hansen
and SAM scores of $i$ stay the same. The 2SFCA score of $i$ falls towards 1, the ratio of centre B,
because centre B is 8 km from $k$ and only the 100 people of $i$ are within its 5 km catchment
(right). The dots mark the example in the five-panel figure above, with 100 people in $i$ and 300
people in $k$.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4
sm_pop <- 10^seq(0, 6, by = 0.05)
sm_vary <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "i", p = c(sm_pop, 100), Hansen = 106.25,
         `2SFCA` = 100 / (p + 300) + 100 / p, SAM = 106.25 / p),
  tibble(panel = "k", p = c(sm_pop, 300), Hansen = 106.25,
         `2SFCA` = 100 / (100 + p) + 1, SAM = 106.25 / 100)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Hansen, `2SFCA`, SAM), names_to = "measure", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(example = (panel == "i" & p == 100) | (panel == "k" & p == 300))
sm_cols <- c(Hansen = "#737373", `2SFCA` = "#3182bd", SAM = "#e6550d")
sm_panel_plot <- function(pan, x_title, show) {
  d <- filter(sm_vary, panel == pan)
  fig <- plotly::plot_ly()
  for (m in names(sm_cols)) {
    fig <- fig |>
      plotly::add_lines(data = filter(d, measure == m, !example), x = ~p, y = ~score, name = m,
                        legendgroup = m, showlegend = show,
                        line = list(color = sm_cols[[m]], width = 3),
                        hovertemplate = paste0(m, "<br>people = %{x:,.0f}<br>score of i = %{y:.4g}",
                                               "<extra></extra>")) |>
      plotly::add_markers(data = filter(d, measure == m, example), x = ~p, y = ~score,
                          legendgroup = m, showlegend = FALSE,
                          marker = list(color = sm_cols[[m]], size = 10),
                          hovertemplate = paste0(m, " in the figure's example<br>score of i = ",
                                                 "%{y:.4g}<extra></extra>"))
  }
  plotly::layout(fig, xaxis = list(type = "log", title = x_title, tickvals = 10^(0:6),
                              ticktext = c("1", "10", "100", "1,000", "10,000", "100,000", "1,000,000")),
                 yaxis = list(type = "log", title = "score of hexagon i", tickvals = 10^(-4:2),
                              ticktext = c("0.0001", "0.001", "0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", "100")))
}
plotly::subplot(sm_panel_plot("i", "people in hexagon i (k has 300)", TRUE),
                sm_panel_plot("k", "people in hexagon k (i has 100)", FALSE),
                nrows = 1, shareY = TRUE, titleX = TRUE, margin = 0.03) |>
  plotly::layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12))
```

| Measure | Unit of the score | The input it adds |
|-------------------------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1. Nearest centre | kilometres | nothing: only the closest centre counts |
| 2. Hansen | none | the capacity of every centre |
| 3. 2SFCA | capacity per person | the people within 5 km of a centre, who share its capacity |
| 4. KD2SFCA | capacity per person | a weight that falls with distance inside the 5 km catchment |
| SAM (side branch) | none | the people of the hexagon itself, as the divisor of its score |

The 300 people of hexagon $k$ lower the capacity per person of centre A in panels 3 and 4. The
weights in panel 4 are $1 - (d/5)^2$, the kernel of Dai and Wang (2011) without its factor 3/4. The
factor cancels between step 1 and step 2. The weight in `ac()` is $e^{-d^2}$, which has no parameter
that sets how fast the weight falls (section 3.2). Panels 2 and 5 use the power function $1/d^2$ of
Hansen (1959). With `ac(family = "Hansen")`, which uses $e^{-2d}$ (section 3.1.1), hexagon $i$
scores $100 e^{-2} + 100 e^{-8} =$ `r round(100 * exp(-2) + 100 * exp(-8), 2)`, against 106.25 in
panel 2.

of Part 1 are checked. In sections 4.4 to 4.6, methods and demand data that the chapter does not use
are added.

| 4.2 | Write out what `ac()` computes for each family, and compare the formulas with those of the slides and the readings | slides 8, 19, 25 to 29; Hansen (1959); Luo and Wang (2003); Polzin et al. (2014); Cheng et al. (2016); Kalogirou and Foley (2006) |
